hints.title: Two Distinct Metric Queries with Union All
hints.text: The problem requires finding the user who rated the most movies, and the movie with the highest average rating in February 2020.

hints.title: Tie-Breaking via Lexicographical Order
hints.text: Sort first by metric descending (count or avg rating), and break ties by name alphabetically in ascending order.

hints.title: Union All Limit Blueprint
hints.text: (select u.name as results from Users u join MovieRating mr on u.user_id = mr.user_id group by u.user_id, u.name order by count(*) desc, u.name asc limit 1) union all (select m.title as results from Movies m join MovieRating mr on m.movie_id = mr.movie_id where mr.created_at between "2020-02-01" and "2020-02-29" group by m.movie_id, m.title order by avg(mr.rating) desc, m.title asc limit 1).

hints.title: Complete Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
(SELECT u.name AS results
 FROM Users u
 JOIN MovieRating mr ON u.user_id = mr.user_id
 GROUP BY u.user_id, u.name
 ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC, u.name ASC
 LIMIT 1)
UNION ALL
(SELECT m.title AS results
 FROM Movies m
 JOIN MovieRating mr ON m.movie_id = mr.movie_id
 WHERE mr.created_at BETWEEN '2020-02-01' AND '2020-02-29'
 GROUP BY m.movie_id, m.title
 ORDER BY AVG(mr.rating) DESC, m.title ASC
 LIMIT 1);
```

complexity.notes: Two independent group aggregations with top-1 limits united into a 2-row result set.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Using simple UNION instead of UNION ALL deduplicates if the top user and movie have identical names.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Parenthesized sub-queries with LIMIT 1 execute the two independent rankings concurrently.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use of UNION ALL and separate group aggregations with tie-breaking.

import pandas as pd

def movie_rating(movies: pd.DataFrame, users: pd.DataFrame, movie_rating: pd.DataFrame) -> pd.DataFrame:
    # 1. Top user
    u_counts = movie_rating.groupby('user_id').size().reset_index(name='cnt')
    u_merged = u_counts.merge(users, on='user_id')
    u_sorted = u_merged.sort_values(by=['cnt', 'name'], ascending=[False, True])
    top_user = u_sorted.iloc[0]['name']

    # 2. Top movie in Feb 2020
    feb = movie_rating[movie_rating['created_at'].astype(str).str.startswith('2020-02')]
    m_avg = feb.groupby('movie_id')['rating'].mean().reset_index()
    m_merged = m_avg.merge(movies, on='movie_id')
    m_sorted = m_merged.sort_values(by=['rating', 'title'], ascending=[False, True])
    top_movie = m_sorted.iloc[0]['title']

    return pd.DataFrame({'results': [top_user, top_movie]})
solutions.approach: Pandas Independent Metric Sorts and Concatenation
